utterances.text: The bridge video Your Honours will be given exhibit number D259 and the document containing the Islamic Declaration will be given Exhibit D260.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Then the parties were also invited to agree upon a date by which any documentation or sentencing testimonial would be filed. Have the parties agreed on a date?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would suggest the same dates as we agreed on the other matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is acceptable, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now I have to -- wasn't that the 18th of August to be filed and any --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It was the 10th, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 10th, yes, and then the 12th for any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber accepts this proposal and reminds the parties what was earlier said about late filing and consequences for final briefs and final argument, that it should not later on become a reason not to follow the scheduling in that respect. Then the Chamber informs the parties that, apart from what we made minor mistakes which now and then causes the Registry to return decisions to us because there are three different dates on it, things like that, but that I signed a decision on exhibits today and it's expected to be filed, a decision which would include a decision on briefly said the Karadzic notebook and the Karadzic letter. So the parties can consult and take note of that decision which has been a written decision. Is there any other practical matter at this moment to be raised, apart from --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Not on behalf of the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, just this. Just briefly before Your Honours came into court, Mr. Krajisnik had mentioned to me that from the CDs which he had produced in the course of his evidence, he has in mind about -- he told me about a dozen documents that he would like to be put in evidence. Your Honour, that's as much as I know because we haven't had a chance to discuss or consider specifically what they are. So I pass that on, Your Honour. Whether they would go in as -- whether they can constitute contextual documents. It's a bit difficult for me to say, Your Honour, because I only know what I've just told Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I take it that Mr. Stewart is well informed. My question is: Would there be a possibility for Defence counsel to find out, together with Mr. Krajisnik, before he returns perhaps to the UNDU, whether they are clearly identified because the first thing would be to identify what documents exactly we are talking about, then it could be considered that the same time limits would be set for both filing, perhaps these documents as tendered as contextual exhibits, and that there would be another two days for the Prosecution to object to any admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With the only caveat being the size of the documents, the numbers appear to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the other question, of course, would be whether they are -- in what language they are. Mr. Krajisnik, could you tell us, the documents you identified as so important that you'd like to have them in evidence, are they in -- is an English translation available?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are English translations for many of them. As for the due date, so to speak, if there are no English translations then they don't even have to be admitted into evidence. Those documents, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I then at this moment leave it to Defence counsel to seek contact with Mr. Krajisnik to see whether the documents can be identified and then select those documents already translated into English and to look after it that on behalf of Mr. Krajisnik these documents will be filed, or at least disclosed, not that this material is not yet disclosed to the Prosecution, but that the Prosecution knows and receives copies or at least such an indication that they can find the material either on the CDs so that they can consider whether they would like to object to admission into evidence of those documents, and -- one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And keeping in mind that the recess might cause some problems in finalising formalities, as far as filing is concerned, the Chamber will not, for those purposes only, that is that formalities are not finalised yet, will not for that reason decide not to admit the documents. So most important for the Chamber is that the Prosecution is well aware by the 10th of August what these documents are, only documents with an English translation, that the Prosecution then has a -- until the 12th of August to make any objections. Of course, the Chamber will then give a decision. But if, for example, the formal filing would not have been completed by the 10th of October due to practical problems which might arise out of the recess, then the Chamber will not consider them as of such importance that they should oppose the admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour did say October. Clearly meant August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It means that -- and that perhaps then is my last point. Unless there is anything else to be raised at this moment. No further matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wanted to say that this mistake clearly indicates that everyone needs perhaps a bit of rest, although it might not be a complete rest because counsel remain counsel even during the holidays. Judges remain judges even during the holidays. Nevertheless, I wish everyone the rest they need at this moment. We will adjourn and we'll proceed in accordance with the scheduling as set by the Chamber before, which means that apart from filings, that we would be in this courtroom again on Tuesday, the 29th of August, in the afternoon. We then sit at Wednesday, the 30th of August, in the morning, and on the 31st of August in the afternoon, always this courtroom, for closing argument. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of August, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24
